data.name: Pad Thai with Tofu Vegetarian
data.description: Pad Thai with Tofu is a classic Thai stir-fried noodle dish made vegetarian by substituting traditional meat with tofu, featuring a flavorful tamarind-based sauce and garnished with peanuts and fresh herbs.
instructions: Drain the tofu and press to remove excess moisture, then cut into bite-sized cubes.
Cook the rice noodles according to package instructions until soft but still slightly firm, then drain and set aside.
Heat vegetable oil in a large wok or skillet over medium-high heat.
Add tofu cubes and stir-fry until golden on all sides, then remove and set aside.
In the same wok, sauté garlic and shallot until fragrant and translucent.
Add soaked rice noodles, tamarind paste, soy sauce, and palm sugar to the wok, tossing to combine and coat the noodles evenly.
Push noodles to the side and crack the eggs into the empty space, scrambling until just set, then mix with the noodles.
Add the tofu back into the wok and toss everything together gently.
Add bean sprouts and spring onion, mix briefly just to warm through.
Serve immediately, garnished with chopped peanuts, lime wedges, and fresh cilantro.
Optionally, serve with chili flakes on the side for added heat.

data.name: Shojin Ryori (Buddhist Vegetarian Cuisine)
data.description: Shojin Ryori is a traditional Japanese Buddhist vegetarian cuisine emphasizing simple, balanced, and seasonal ingredients, prepared without meat or strong flavors to promote purity and mindfulness.
instructions: Prepare all vegetables by washing and cutting them into bite-sized pieces as appropriate.
Soak kombu in water for about 30 minutes to make dashi stock, then slowly heat the kombu water without boiling to extract umami, removing kombu before the water boils.
Slice konnyaku thinly and blanch in boiling water for a few minutes to remove its odor and soften it.
Heat a pan and lightly toast sesame seeds until fragrant, setting aside for garnish.
Lightly sauté root vegetables such as carrot and daikon radish in a small amount of sesame oil until slightly tender.
Add the prepared dashi stock, simmer vegetables gently until fully cooked but firm to the bite.
Add tofu and simmer gently to absorb flavors.
Season with soy sauce, mirin, and a pinch of salt, tasting carefully to maintain balance and subtlety.
Arrange the cooked vegetables and tofu artfully on a serving dish, garnishing with toasted sesame seeds and fresh shiso leaf if available.

data.name: Vegetarian Chili
data.description: A hearty and flavorful meat-free chili packed with vegetables and beans, perfect for a nutritious and comforting meal.
instructions: Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Add chopped onion, bell pepper, and garlic; sauté until softened.
Stir in chopped carrot and zucchini, cook for 5 minutes.
Add canned diced tomato, kidney beans, black beans, and corn to the pot.
Pour in vegetable broth and stir to combine.
Season with chili powder, cumin, smoked paprika, salt, and black pepper.
Bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer uncovered for 30 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Adjust seasoning to taste and serve hot, garnished with fresh cilantro if desired.

data.name: Vegetarian Mapo Tofu
data.description: Vegetarian Mapo Tofu is a plant-based version of the classic Sichuan spicy tofu dish with a flavorful, spicy, and numbing sauce made from fermented bean paste and Sichuan peppercorns.
instructions: Drain the tofu and cut it into 2 cm cubes. Set aside.
Heat vegetable oil in a pan over medium heat. Add minced garlic, minced ginger, and chopped green onion whites. Sauté until fragrant.
Add doubanjiang (spicy fermented bean paste) and stir-fry for about 1 minute to release aroma.
Add vegetable broth and bring to a simmer.
Gently add tofu cubes to the broth and simmer for 5 minutes to absorb flavors.
Mix the cornstarch with water to make a slurry.
Slowly stir in the cornstarch slurry to the pan, gently stirring to thicken the sauce without breaking the tofu.
Add soy sauce, sugar, and a pinch of ground Sichuan peppercorns. Adjust seasoning to taste.
Add chopped green onion greens and a drizzle of sesame oil. Stir gently.
Serve hot over steamed rice.
